s0201.literal: Shortly he was made Shouguang academician and Director of Righteousness, then again removed to criminal-prison adviser in the Prince of Wuling's western headquarters.
s0201.idiomatic: Shortly he was made Shouguang academician and director of righteousness, then criminal-prison adviser in the prince of Wuling's western headquarters.

s0202.literal: In the first year of Taiqing he memorialized requesting trial office and was made magistrate of Nansha.
s0202.idiomatic: In Taiqing year 1 he memorialized to enter trial office and was made magistrate of Nansha.

s0203.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Zhijing led his command to rush to relieve the capital.
s0203.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Zhijing led his troops to relieve the capital.

s0204.literal: Reaching the commandery border, hearing the terrace city had fallen, he with his forces took leave and returned to his home district.
s0204.idiomatic: At the commandery border he heard the terrace city had fallen; he bade his men farewell and returned home.

s0205.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng he was made recording secretary in the Pacification-hui Prince of Jin'an's household.
s0205.idiomatic: In Chengsheng year 2 he was recording secretary in the pacification-hui prince of Jin'an's household.

s0206.literal: At that time Xiao Bo held Lingbiao; an edict ordered Zhijing to proclaim the intent and comfort him. When Jiangling fell he still remained at Guangzhou.
s0206.idiomatic: Xiao Bo then held Lingbiao; Zhijing was ordered to proclaim the edict and reassure him. When Jiangling fell he stayed at Guangzhou.

s0207.literal: Early in Taijian he returned to court and was appointed eastern-palace righteousness-bureau scholar; the crown prince had long heard his name and especially lowered himself to honor and receive him.
s0207.idiomatic: Early in Taijian he returned to court as an eastern-palace righteousness-bureau scholar; the crown prince had long known his name and treated him with special favor.

s0208.literal: He was in succession promoted recording secretary in the Prince of Poyang's central guard headquarters, recorder within limits in the pacify-north headquarters, Southern Terrace investigating secretary attendant drafting reports, and staff adviser in the campaign-south headquarters.
s0208.idiomatic: He rose through recording secretary in the prince of Poyang's central guard, recorder within limits in the pacify-north headquarters, southern terrace investigating secretary, and staff adviser in the campaign-south headquarters.

s0209.literal: Zhijing at first advanced through classical studies, yet broadly traversed literature and history, elegantly possessed literary brush, and was not an orthodox Confucian.
s0209.idiomatic: Zhijing had entered through classical studies but ranged widely in literature and history, wrote well, and was no orthodox Confucian.

s0210.literal: By nature modest and cautious, he never used talent and learning to condescend to others; he received and guided juniors, ever earnest and agreeable.
s0210.idiomatic: Modest and cautious by nature, he never flaunted his learning; he welcomed juniors and was always earnest and kindly.

s0211.literal: On each anniversary of a parent's death he kept vegetarian observance, personally sprinkling and sweeping, weeping the whole day—gentlemen deemed him for earnest conduct.
s0211.idiomatic: On each parent's anniversary he kept a vegetarian observance, swept the shrine himself, and wept all day; gentlemen praised his earnest conduct.

s0212.literal: In the eleventh year he died, aged sixty-one.
s0212.idiomatic: He died in year 11, aged sixty-one.

s0213.literal: The crown prince sighed in regret and sent funeral gifts very generously.
s0213.idiomatic: The crown prince mourned him and sent lavish funeral gifts.

s0214.literal: He had a collection of ten juan circulating in the world.
s0214.idiomatic: A collection of ten juan by him circulated.

s0215.literal: His son Dekun had his father's manner and reached office as recording secretary to the Wu-xing Prince of the central army.
s0215.idiomatic: His son Dekun had his father's manner and became recording secretary to the Wu-xing prince of the central army.

s0216.literal: Lu Yan, styled Wenyu, was a younger cousin of Minister of Personnel Qiong.
s0216.idiomatic: Lu Yan, styled Wenyu, was a younger cousin of Minister of Personnel Qiong.

s0217.literal: His father Linggong was Liang recording secretary in the Prince of Xuancheng's central army headquarters.
s0217.idiomatic: His father Linggong was Liang recording secretary in the prince of Xuancheng's central army headquarters.

s0218.literal: Yan from childhood was orphaned, loved learning, and had resolve and integrity.
s0218.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Yan loved learning and had firm resolve.

s0219.literal: The province nominated him as outstanding candidate.
s0219.idiomatic: The province nominated him as an outstanding candidate.

s0220.literal: On leaving the dark he was made acting secretary to the Pacification-hui Prince of Shixing, was in succession promoted to outer-army legal adviser, and straight academician of Jiadé Hall.
s0220.idiomatic: On entering office he was acting secretary to the pacification-hui prince of Shixing, then outer-army legal adviser and a straight academician of Jiadé Hall.

s0221.literal: In his spare moments from audiences Emperor Wen paid considerable attention to historical records; because Yan was erudite and skilled at recitation, he was placed at his side.
s0221.idiomatic: In spare moments from audiences Emperor Wen attended to historical records; finding Yan erudite and skilled at recitation, he kept him close.

s0222.literal: Once he was ordered to compose an inscription for a knife; Yan took brush and finished at once without any emendation. Emperor Wen admired him long and granted one suit of robes.
s0222.idiomatic: Once ordered to compose a knife inscription, Yan wrote it at a stroke without emendation. Emperor Wen admired him at length and granted a suit of robes.

s0223.literal: Shortly he was additionally made Regular Attendant through Direct Communication of the Scattered Cavalry, deputy to the Prince of Langya on a mission to hire Qi; when they reached Ye, Hou fell ill and died, and Yan himself became head of the mission.
s0223.idiomatic: Shortly he was also regular attendant through direct communication of the scattered cavalry, deputy to the prince of Langya on a mission to Qi; at Ye Hou fell ill and died, and Yan himself headed the mission.

s0224.literal: He was then just over twenty; spirit and bearing were bright and clear, responses in audience relaxed and keen—the great officials of Qi very much inclined their hearts to him.
s0224.idiomatic: He was then just over twenty, bright in spirit and bearing, quick and poised in reply; Qi officials greatly favored him.

s0225.literal: On return he was registrar of the Cloud-Banner Prince of Xin'an, promoted to chief steward of the Prince of Ancheng, [18] and recorder of the Ningyuan headquarters.
s0225.idiomatic: On return he was registrar to the cloud-banner prince of Xin'an, then chief steward to the prince of Ancheng, [18] and recorder of the Ningyuan headquarters.

s0226.literal: Early in Taijian he was merit-clerk of the Bright Prestige headquarters for the Prince of Wuling and concurrently eastern-palace recorder.
s0226.idiomatic: Early in Taijian he was merit-clerk in the bright-prestige headquarters of the prince of Wuling and concurrently eastern-palace recorder.

s0227.literal: On his mother's mourning he left office.
s0227.idiomatic: He left office on his mother's mourning.

s0228.literal: In the fifth year he died, aged thirty-four.
s0228.idiomatic: He died in year 5, aged thirty-four.

s0229.literal: The crown prince deeply mourned him, personally ordered mourning rites, increased funeral gifts, and himself composed an epitaph inscription.
s0229.idiomatic: The crown prince mourned him deeply, ordered mourning by personal edict, increased funeral gifts, and wrote the epitaph himself.

s0230.literal: In the second year of Zhide he was posthumously made Director of the Court for Imperial Granaries.
s0230.idiomatic: In Zhide year 2 he was posthumously made director of the court for imperial granaries.

s0231.literal: Yan had few desires and rarely competed for acclaim; his mind roamed classical texts, at ease.
s0231.idiomatic: Yan had few desires and rarely strove; his mind dwelt in the classics, at ease.

s0232.literal: Most of the writings he produced did not survive in the originals; Hou Zhu sought his surviving texts and compiled them into two juan.
s0232.idiomatic: Most of his writings did not survive; Hou Zhu sought his remnants and compiled two juan.

s0233.literal: He had a younger brother Yu.
s0233.idiomatic: He had a younger brother Yu.

s0236.literal: From youth he was devoted to study and fine in literary craft.
s0236.idiomatic: From youth he studied devotedly and wrote finely.

s0237.literal: The province nominated him as outstanding candidate.
s0237.idiomatic: The province nominated him as an outstanding candidate.

s0238.literal: On leaving the dark he was made acting secretary to the Swift-cavalry Prince of Ancheng, transferred to army staff adviser for the Prince of Jin'an, and eastern-palace academician.
s0238.idiomatic: On entering office he was acting secretary to the swift-cavalry prince of Ancheng, then staff adviser to the prince of Jin'an and an eastern-palace academician.

s0239.literal: When his elder brother Yan was then recorder, both with talent and learning amused and attended left and right; people at the time compared them to the two Yings.
s0239.idiomatic: When his elder brother Yan was recorder, both entertained the heir with their learning; contemporaries compared them to the two Yings.

s0240.literal: In the second year of Taijian the crown prince performed the offering at the imperial academy; palace officials all composed poems, and Yu was ordered to write the preface—the text very rich and elegant.
s0240.idiomatic: In Taijian year 2 the crown prince offered at the imperial academy; palace officials all wrote poems, and Yu was ordered to compose the preface in rich, elegant prose.

s0241.literal: He was moved to bureau director of sacrifices in the Masters of Writing and on his mother's mourning left office.
s0241.idiomatic: He was made bureau director of sacrifices in the masters of writing, then left office on his mother's mourning.

s0242.literal: When mourning ended he was merit-clerk of the Bright Prestige general headquarters for the Prince of Guiyang and concurrently eastern-palace recorder.
s0242.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was merit-clerk in the bright-prestige headquarters of the prince of Guiyang and concurrently eastern-palace recorder.

s0243.literal: He was in succession promoted literary scholar for the Prince of Yongyang, palace rhetorician, and attendant within the palace.
s0243.idiomatic: He rose through literary scholar to the prince of Yongyang, palace rhetorician, and palace attendant.

s0244.literal: Yu from childhood always read books day and night without ceasing, clever and with strong memory—one reading and nothing was lost.
s0244.idiomatic: Yu had read constantly from childhood, day and night; clever and with a strong memory, one reading left nothing lost.

s0245.literal: He once received Zhuangzi and Laozi from Zhou Hongzheng of Runan and learned substantive discourse from the dharma master Monk Tao—both penetrated the great purport.
s0245.idiomatic: He studied Zhuangzi and Laozi under Zhou Hongzheng of Runan and substantive discourse under the dharma master Monk Tao, mastering both.

s0246.literal: At that time the heir apparent loved learning and wished to view all books broadly; because the zi and ji categories were numerous, he ordered Yu to excerpt and compile them—before it was finished Yu died, aged forty-four.
s0246.idiomatic: The heir apparent then loved learning and wished to survey all books; the zi and ji categories being vast, he ordered Yu to excerpt them, but Yu died before finishing, aged forty-four.

s0247.literal: The crown prince wept for him, personally ordered mourning, the government supplied the funeral, and also personally composed sacrificial text and sent an envoy to offer condolence sacrifices.
s0247.idiomatic: The crown prince wept for him, ordered mourning by personal edict, supplied the funeral from government funds, composed a sacrificial text, and sent an envoy to mourn.

s0248.literal: [19] He still wrote to Chamberlain Jiang Zong, saying: "Recorder Lu Yu has suddenly collapsed and transformed; grief, mourning, and cherishing—when will this feeling end?
s0248.idiomatic: [19] He also wrote to chamberlain Jiang Zong: "Recorder Lu Yu has suddenly died; grief and mourning—when can it end?

s0249.literal: My lifelong loves—you all know them; I myself consider my learning in Ru elegance not to reach the ancients, yet cherishing the worthy and admiring scholars—that feeling is especially deep.
s0249.idiomatic: You know my lifelong pursuits; I find my Ru learning falls short of the ancients, yet in cherishing the worthy and admiring scholars my feeling runs especially deep.

s0250.literal: The Liang house was in turmoil and separation, the realm seethed; books and histories were incomplete, rites and music collapsed; among later-born later-learners it is not that none face the wall—but to stand out from the crowd, only this man.
s0250.idiomatic: The Liang house was torn apart and the realm boiled; books and histories were broken, rites and music ruined; later students are not without learning by rote, but to stand out from the crowd—only this man.

s0251.literal: Though my knowledge and view are narrow, I have never lent my voice in discussion to others; yet toward a scrap of virtue or a small talent I especially sigh in admiration.
s0251.idiomatic: My knowledge is narrow and I have never lent my voice in debate, yet toward the smallest talent I always sighed in admiration.

s0252.literal: How much more for vast knowledge and extraordinary talent—this is truly a place where words are forgotten.
s0252.idiomatic: How much more for vast learning and rare talent—here words fail.

s0253.literal: Discussing his comprehensive mastery of the zi and shi, thorough study of Ru and Mo, nothing that reached his ear was lost, nothing his eye met but he could recite it—one praise, one blame, one stirring, one lifting; discoursing on the mysterious and analyzing principle, splitting texts and plucking sentences—never did the hearer not submit in heart or the listener unknit the cheeks; when meanings met, he reckoned it the reward of a plain-clothed friendship.
s0253.idiomatic: In mastering zi and shi, in Ru and Mo, nothing heard was lost and nothing seen went unrecited; praise and blame, stir and lift, discourse on mystery and analysis of principle, splitting texts and plucking lines—hearers submitted and listeners smiled; when minds met, it was the reward of friendship among plain cloth.

s0254.literal: In the leisure of my oversight duties, in the gaps between affairs, I quite used witty talk to soothe feeling, zithers and wine cups at ease, elegant pieces and lush stanzas rising in interchange like crossed blades.
s0254.idiomatic: In the leisure of oversight, in gaps between affairs, we used wit to soothe the mood, zithers and cups at ease, elegant verses and lush stanzas crossing like blades.

s0255.literal: Whenever wind was clear and moon bright, scenery fine and season apt, facing the mountains' uneven heights and gazing at the great waves' vast overflow—or playing with fresh flowers, or watching fallen leaves, now hearing spring birds, now listening to autumn geese—never did we not bend knees and raise cups, join feeling and send forth compositions, taking turns at polishing, interspersed with banter, all pleasing ear and eye and alike staying in sentiment.
s0255.idiomatic: Under clear wind and bright moon, fine scenes and apt seasons, facing jagged mountains and vast waves, playing with fresh flowers or watching fallen leaves, hearing spring birds or autumn geese—we always bent knee and raised cup, joined feeling and sent forth lines, polishing in turn with banter between, pleasing ear and eye and holding feeling alike.

s0256.literal: I myself thought a hundred years swift and morning dew cause for sorrow—who expected jade broken and orchid snapped, suddenly to follow a short fate? For grief and for regret, what more can be said?
s0256.idiomatic: I thought a hundred years swift and morning dew a cause for sorrow—who expected jade to break and orchid to snap, suddenly cut off? For grief and regret, what more can be said?

s0257.literal: Traces and surviving writings—each sight increases tears; breaking the lute-string and casting aside the brush, I constantly have sour regret.
s0257.idiomatic: Traces and surviving writings move me to tears at every sight; breaking the lute-string and casting aside the brush, I constantly feel sour regret.

s0258.literal: [20] As you share the same intent, I briefly set forth my feelings; tears have no outlet, words cannot write the meaning."
s0258.idiomatic: [20] As you share this intent I briefly lay out my feelings; tears have no outlet and words cannot hold the meaning."

s0259.literal: People of the time esteemed him thus.
s0259.idiomatic: People of the time esteemed him thus.

s0260.literal: In the second year of Zhide he was posthumously made Director of the Palace for Imperial Luminaries.
s0260.idiomatic: In Zhide year 2 he was posthumously made director of the palace for imperial luminaries.

s0261.literal: He had a collection of ten juan.
s0261.idiomatic: He left a collection of ten juan.

s0262.literal: Yu had an elder cousin's son Jie and a younger cousin's son Chen.
s0262.idiomatic: Yu had an elder cousin's son Jie and a younger cousin's son Chen.

s0263.literal: Jie, styled Runyu, was son of Liang Director of the Grand Master of Works Yanzi [21].
s0263.idiomatic: Jie, styled Runyu, was son of Liang director of the grand master of works Yanzi [21].

s0264.literal: [21] Refined and magnanimous in discernment, fond of learning, able to compose prose.
s0264.idiomatic: [21] Refined and discerning, fond of learning, able to write prose.

s0265.literal: Nominated as outstanding candidate, in policy essay he ranked high.
s0265.idiomatic: Nominated as outstanding candidate, he ranked high in the policy essay.

s0266.literal: Minister of Personnel Yuan Shu recommended him to Emperor Wen; he was specially appointed literary scholar to the Prince of Hengyang and straight academician of Tianbao Hall.
s0266.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Yuan Shu recommended him to Emperor Wen; he was specially made literary scholar to the prince of Hengyang and straight academician of Tianbao Hall.

s0267.literal: Early in Taijian he was moved to friend of the Prince of Changsha and concurrently recorder.
s0267.idiomatic: Early in Taijian he became friend to the prince of Changsha and concurrently recorder.

s0268.literal: When Hou Zhu was in the Eastern Palace he heard Jie's fame and summoned him as recorder.
s0268.idiomatic: When Hou Zhu was in the eastern palace he heard of Jie and summoned him as recorder.

s0269.literal: He was then made attendant within the palace, recorder as before, and greatly favored and treated with intimacy.
s0269.idiomatic: He was then made palace attendant, still recorder, and greatly favored.

s0270.literal: Shortly, through illness he lost his sight; about to return to his home district, the crown prince removed his own garment to give Jie and wept for him.
s0270.idiomatic: Soon illness blinded him; as he was to return home the crown prince gave him his own garment and wept.

s0271.literal: In the eighth year he died, aged thirty-seven.
s0271.idiomatic: He died in year 8, aged thirty-seven.

s0272.literal: There was an order to observe mourning and funeral gifts were also increased.
s0272.idiomatic: An edict ordered mourning and increased funeral gifts.

s0273.literal: In the second year of Zhide he was posthumously made Director of the Palace for the Imperial Treasury.
s0273.idiomatic: In Zhide year 2 he was posthumously made director of the palace for the imperial treasury.

s0274.literal: He had a collection of ten juan.
s0274.idiomatic: He left a collection of ten juan.

s0275.literal: Chen, styled Jieyu, was son of Chief Steward Qiu of the Pacification-steadfast Prince of Linchuan's household.
s0275.idiomatic: Chen, styled Jieyu, was son of chief steward Qiu in the pacification-steadfast prince of Linchuan's household.

s0276.literal: From youth alert and talented, he served his stepmother and was famed for filial piety.
s0276.idiomatic: Alert and talented from youth, he was famed for serving his stepmother filially.

s0277.literal: When Emperor Wen was administrator of Kuaiji, Chen was eighteen; he submitted a eulogy on good government, very rich in literary color, and thereby became famous and was nominated as outstanding candidate.
s0277.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was Kuaiji administrator, Chen at eighteen submitted a eulogy on good government of fine literary color, won fame, and was nominated as outstanding candidate.

s0278.literal: On first taking office he was registrar to the Prince of Hengyang and concurrently eastern-palace recorder.
s0278.idiomatic: On first taking office he was registrar to the prince of Hengyang and concurrently eastern-palace recorder.

s0279.literal: He served in succession as literary scholar to the Prince of Yuzhang, concurrently recorder, registrar of the Minister of State, and straight academician of Xuanming Hall.
s0279.idiomatic: He served as literary scholar to the prince of Yuzhang with concurrent recorder, minister of state registrar, and straight academician of Xuanming Hall.

s0280.literal: Shortly he was moved to vice director of the Three Excellencies in the Masters of Writing, concurrently Regular Attendant through Direct Communication of the Scattered Cavalry, on a mission to hire Qi; on return he was left western aide of the Minister of State.
s0280.idiomatic: Shortly he was vice director of the three excellencies in the masters of writing and regular attendant through direct communication on a mission to Qi; on return he was left western aide of the minister of state.

s0281.literal: He again held charge of the eastern-palace recorder; the crown prince loved Chen's talent in debate and treated him with deep courtesy.
s0281.idiomatic: He again held the eastern-palace recorder; the crown prince loved his eloquence and treated him with deep courtesy.

s0282.literal: When Hou Zhu succeeded to the throne he was moved to Supervisor of Attendants of the Yellow Gate and Secretariat Drafter Within the Palace, participating in confidential matters.
s0282.idiomatic: When Hou Zhu succeeded he was made supervisor of attendants of the yellow gate and secretariat drafter within the palace, sharing confidential affairs.

s0283.literal: Chen's nature was rather careless; he sat convicted of leaking forbidden-palace speech and was by edict granted death, aged forty-two.
s0283.idiomatic: Careless by nature, he was convicted of leaking palace secrets and was ordered to die, aged forty-two.

s0285.literal: He Zhiyuan was a native of Qian in Lujiang.
s0285.idiomatic: He Zhiyuan came from Qian in Lujiang.

s0286.literal: His grandfather Sengda was Qi investigating secretary attendant drafting reports of the Southern Terrace.
s0286.idiomatic: His grandfather Sengda was Qi investigating secretary of the southern terrace.

s0287.literal: His father Fasheng was famed for moral conduct.
s0287.idiomatic: His father Fasheng was famed for moral conduct.

s0288.literal: Zhiyuan from youth loved learning and had literary thought; in mourning his observance exceeded the rites, and he was valued by Liang Minister of Works Yuan Ang.
s0288.idiomatic: Zhiyuan loved learning from youth and had literary gifts; his mourning observance exceeded the rites, and Liang Minister of Works Yuan Ang valued him.

s0289.literal: At the end of the Tianjian era Ang memorialized recommending him, and he thereby obtained an audience.
s0289.idiomatic: At the end of Tianjian Ang memorialized recommending him, and he was summoned to audience.

s0290.literal: On leaving the dark he was made aide in the discussion bureau of Liang Grand Marshal the Prince of Linchuan's Yangzhou separate office, and shortly transferred to chief secretary.
s0290.idiomatic: On entering office he was aide in the discussion bureau of Liang grand marshal the prince of Linchuan's Yangzhou separate office, then chief secretary.

s0291.literal: When Ang became administrator of Danyang he summoned Zhiyuan as aide of the five offices of Danyang, in overall charge of the household-registration bureau.
s0291.idiomatic: When Ang became Danyang administrator he summoned Zhiyuan as aide of the five Danyang offices, overseeing the household-registration bureau.

s0292.literal: Shortly he was made magistrate of Xinyi.
s0292.idiomatic: Shortly he was made magistrate of Xinyi.

s0293.literal: Among Zhiyuan's clansmen was Jingrong, whose power and position were weighty; he repeatedly paid calls, but Zhiyuan in the end never went to him.
s0293.idiomatic: His clansman Jingrong held weighty power and rank and called on him often, but Zhiyuan never returned the visits.

s0294.literal: Someone asked the reason; Zhiyuan said: "In olden days a man of Chu won favor through Guan Qi, and those who had horses all perished.
s0294.idiomatic: Asked why, Zhiyuan said, "Long ago a Chu man won favor through Guan Qi, and everyone who had horses perished.

s0295.literal: When virtue is thin and position weighty, ruin is near; I fear I would not gain the benefit but would invite the calamity."
s0295.idiomatic: When virtue is thin and office heavy, downfall is near; I fear I would gain no benefit but invite disaster."

s0296.literal: Men of insight for this praised him.
s0296.idiomatic: The discerning praised him for it.

s0297.literal: When the Anxi Prince of Wuling became inspector of Yizhou, Zhiyuan was made criminal-prison adviser in the Anxi headquarters.
s0297.idiomatic: When the anxi prince of Wuling became Yizhou inspector, Zhiyuan was criminal-prison adviser in the anxi headquarters.

s0298.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion the Prince of Wuling, as Grand Marshal exercising regency, appointed Southern Liang province
s0298.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion the prince of Wuling, as grand marshal exercising regency, appointed him to Southern Liang province

s0300.literal: [inspector] [22] and grand administrator of Northern Baxi.
s0300.idiomatic: inspector [22] and grand administrator of Northern Baxi.
